Commits 9dd97bd (stories) -> 0c331ab (store) -> 128dcca (UTM) -> 42d2b5d (docs) -> 63effa4 (gitignore) -> a3166ac (Vercel correction) -> f88e436 + d20ca56 + 5da52ec (Lighthouse and CSP). Record docs/checkpoints/blank-404s-2026-09-06.md; laws §8.34 a-h; rollback tag pre-blank-404-fix-2026-09-06 = 95ad817. WHAT IT FIXED: four routes answered a 404 with an EMPTY document (<html id="__next_error__">, no stylesheet, no text, no lang) and appeared only after JavaScript hydrated — store.kheelona.com/<typo>, store.kheelona.com/store, kheelona.com/stories/<unknown-slug> (a public marketing URL pattern), and /thanks when a VALIDLY SIGNED link pointed at an order that would not load, i.e. a person who had PAID us. Cause is Next's: a thrown notFound() takes the error path (getErrorRSCPayload) and answers with a client-rendered shell, while a routing-level 404 renders normally — which is why kheelona.com/typo was always fine. No upstream fix; 16.3.4 is latest. §8.34-f, LEARNED BY DEPLOYING: NextResponse.rewrite(url,{status:404}) honours the destination under `next start` and does NOT on Vercel — the edge sees the 4xx, discards the destination and serves its own /404, which here is the MARKETING 404. It shipped that way for one deploy. Tell: x-matched-path: /404. So /stories/[slug] uses dynamicParams=false (routing 404, marketing chrome, correct there) and the store RENDERS at 200 with its own chrome. STORE_PAGES/isStorePage were added for the status and removed with it, so routeForHost is simpler than before the round; /404-store-path is deleted. `next start` is NOT the deployment target, and this repo cannot deploy. §8.34-g/h, ALSO PRODUCTION-ONLY: every measurement tag is host-gated, so Lighthouse had only ever been run locally and read a misleading 96. Production best-practices is 74 against a 90 gate, and has been since the Meta Pixel landed 2026-09-01. Attributed with a control: production with facebook blocked reads 96, +googletagmanager blocked also 96 — the pixel costs 22 points, GA4 zero. FOUNDER DECISION: keep the pixel, accept the score (§8.34-h), because only Performance feeds ranking and that is 100, and dropping the pixel would lose PageView/ViewContent/InitiateCheckout/Lead and weaken Purchase matching (CAPI reads the _fbp cookie the pixel sets). ACCEPTED NUMBER IS 74 NOW, 78 AFTER THE CSP FLIP — not the 81 first predicted: a Lighthouse audit is PASS/FAIL, so clearing 3 of 4 items in an audit moved nothing. CSP: Lighthouse's errors-in-console audit reads Report-Only violations off the console, far faster than the Vercel log, and it was the first time anyone had read them. Three refusals would have broken things on the flip: www.facebook.com missing from frame-src (the pixel's cookie-matching frame) and form-action (fbevents.js falls back to a form POST to /tr), and www.googletagmanager.com from img-src (GA4 beacons from the TAG host). Founder approved all three; they are LIVE, pinned by test/security-headers.test.ts, and form-action carries a comment saying it is the loosest line in the policy and goes if the pixel goes. THE FLIP ITSELF IS STILL OPEN and needs a FRESH observation window — every report before 2026-09-06 was against a policy refusing things we need. completed_in_this_session: META CONVERSIONS API for Purchase, server-side (§8.30-l). Sent from notifyPaid, which is reached only behind markPaid returning "paid" - so it inherits exactly-once and never-throw from the receipt email rather than re-earning them. Deduplicated against the browser event by purchaseEventId(orderRef) = purchase_KH-XXXX-XXXX, which both sides derive independently with no shared state.

NO PUBLIC /api/capi ENDPOINT, deliberately, against the guide that asked for one: that route would let anyone on the internet write fake purchases into the ad account, and would have had the browser POST the customer email and phone in the clear to be hashed. Only a purchase Razorpay confirmed can report one, and only SHA-256 leaves.

NEW COLUMN preorders.fb_attrib (nullable jsonb, founder ran the migration 2026-09-02), mirroring how utm was already done. It holds _fbp, _fbc, client IP and user agent, captured in create-order because the webhook is called by Razorpay and carries none of the customer request. ALL read server-side from the request the browser already sends - no client change at all, and no new say for the client.

META_CAPI_TOKEN added to lib/store/env.ts as OPTIONAL (absent = server Purchase skipped, browser pixel carries on) and to test/store-secrets.test.ts as a real secret that may never take a NEXT_PUBLIC_ name. THREE CLAIMS IN THE EXTERNAL REVIEW WERE FALSE about this codebase and were NOT acted on. (1) "Purchase on /thanks has no de-dup guard": there is no pixel call in /thanks at all - Purchase fires in Razorpay success handler, once per payment, so a refresh or an email-link return cannot re-fire it. (2) "Add Lead on contact form submit": /contact has NO form, only WhatsApp and mailto links. (3) "NEXT_PUBLIC_META_PIXEL_ID already set in Vercel / enabled on Preview": no such env var exists, the id is hardcoded, and previews are excluded by the HOSTNAME gate - so previews were never sending events.

REAL DEFECT FIXED from that review: resolveTier returned event_tiers.amount_paise unvalidated, so a 0 or null row rendered a live "Pay ₹0 and reserve" button - and Razorpay REFUSES a ₹0 order, so the parent got a dead button on a payment page with no explanation. Now refused as an invalid tier. Only reachable via a signed event-tier link, never the main store.

⚠ OPEN AND NOT CLAUDE-FIXABLE: Meta Automatic Advanced Matching is ON BY DEFAULT and scrapes the pre-order form, which makes the LIVE /privacy page untrue - it promises no tool is ever sent a name, phone, email or the child age. Founder must either switch AAM off in Events Manager (two clicks, page becomes true again) or ask for §8.30-g to be rewritten a second time. Law recorded as §8.30-m.

PRIVACY REWRITTEN A SECOND TIME, and this one was OUR OWN doing (§8.30-n). The Conversions API shipped 2026-09-02 sends a SHA-256 of the parent email, phone and first name, while /privacy still promised no tool "is ever sent your name, your address, your phone number, your email". Code and sentence shipped a day apart and contradicted each other. Founder chose option B: keep the matching, disclose it. The page now says at pre-order Meta is sent a ONE-WAY CODE made from email, phone and first name, that it cannot be turned back into the details, and that the details themselves are never sent. Two promises survive and are now enforced against meta-capi.ts itself: the delivery address and anything about the child are never sent.

AAM DECIDED: KEPT ON, ALL FIELDS (founder, 2026-09-02, after being recommended off twice). Do not re-raise. Consequence handled the same day: AAM scrapes what Meta's script recognises, including city/state/pincode from the address form on /thanks, so /privacy STOPPED promising "your delivery address is never sent" and "nothing about your child is ever sent". Both are now BANNED by test so they cannot come back while AAM is on. Replacement wording is category-level at the founder's direction ("keep it vague, think like a lawyer") - a legitimate drafting choice, and the line held was that nothing on the page DENIES something that happens. Noted to the founder once: under DPDP §5 a vaguer notice is a weaker position, not a safer one, because clear itemised notice is what evidences notice was given. Page stays counsel-gated. Law §8.30-o.

SETTLED 2026-09-02, and recorded so it stops recurring (§8.30-p): "Purchase fires on /thanks and needs a re-fire guard" is FALSE and was raised THREE times. No guard added, and deliberately NOT logged as a known limitation, because a documented limitation that does not exist gets re-raised every quarter until somebody fixes it. Purchase fires from Razorpay's success handler in PreorderForm.tsx, which never renders on /thanks; that page renders AddressForm, whose only analytics call is addressSaved. WHY IT LOOKS TRUE, and this is the reusable part: Purchase, eventID and thanks all sit in the SAME built JS chunk because Next groups routes into shared chunks - co-location is not a call site. GREP THE SOURCE, NOT THE BUNDLE. Same family as §8.25-bb, where grepping HTML found strings that lived only in the RSC payload. A pointer now sits in the header comment of src/app/store/thanks/page.tsx, which is where the next person looks.

Also settled: preview deployments have never sent pixel events, and the cause is OUR hostname gate (§8.30-b), not Meta's domain allow list. It will not change if that allow list is edited, and production is the only place to test.

OBSERVABILITY FIX after the first real CAPI order (§8.30-q). Marketing asked whether the webhook fired and Meta accepted the event for KH-G7RD-96ZK, and it was UNANSWERABLE - not for lack of access, but because reportPurchaseToMeta logged only failures, so "sent" and "skipped" were both silent. The rule earned: a log that only fires on failure can answer "did it break", never "did it work". Every branch now logs [meta-capi] SENT|SKIPPED|REJECTED|FAILED <event_id>, success carrying events_received and fbtrace_id, skip naming META_CAPI_TOKEN. /api/health gained capi: configured|missing, presence only and never the value, same shape as the existing email field - so "did the env var land after the redeploy" is one curl. Tests assert the token appears in no log line and in no health response.

⚠ NEAR MISS, caught and fixed the same turn, worth remembering. Adding the /api/health capi test, I checked for an existing test with `find -name "*health*test*"`, got nothing, and wrote the file with `cat >`. The file DID exist - as src/app/api/health/route.test.ts, where only the DIRECTORY says health and the filename is route.test.ts - so the name-glob missed it and the redirect silently destroyed FIVE tests, including the two that guard real laws: that /api/health never publishes the paid-order count (§8.26, founder: no public counter) and that it throttles a looping caller (F-07). The replacement even mocked out rate-limit, which would have made the throttle tests unwritable. WHAT CAUGHT IT: the test count came out 946 when the arithmetic said 951, and chasing that five-test gap instead of accepting a green suite is what surfaced it - the destroyed tests were the difference. Restored from git and the two new ones merged in properly. LESSONS: in this repo a route test is <dir>/route.test.ts, so glob on the PATH not the filename; check `git ls-files` or `ls` the directory before writing; never `cat >` a path not confirmed absent; and a test COUNT that does not reconcile is a finding, not noise.

TWO INDEPENDENT QA AGENTS, and both earned their keep. The first reviewed the shipped Meta work and found 10 issues; the second reviewed my PLAN to fix them and rejected three parts of it. THE MOST IMPORTANT CATCH WAS IN MY OWN PLAN: I had the not-payable check running before the already-paid check, and `paid` is not in the allow-list, so it would have logged an error and returned the alarm outcome on EVERY successful order - two paths reach markPaid and the second lands in that branch by design. The alarm would have been buried in false positives from day one. No test would have caught it; plan review did.

🔴 FIXED: a refunded or CANCELLED order could be resurrected and shipped (§8.30-s). markPaid guarded with .neq("status","paid"), which reads as "not already paid" but the statuses are created|paid|failed|refunded|cancelled, so refunded AND cancelled both satisfied it. A webhook retry after a refund flipped the row back to paid, putting a refunded customer BACK IN THE DISPATCH QUEUE (status=paid IS the queue), plus a second receipt and a duplicate Purchase. §8.25-ee from the opposite direction. Now .in("status",["created","failed"]) on both the main UPDATE and orphan recovery, a distinct not-payable outcome, and alertNotPayable emails env.alertEmail INTERNAL ONLY - never notifyPaid, which would tell the refunded customer their order is live again. cancelled is the worse half: it is only ever set by hand, so a human decision could be undone by a retry.

🔴 FIXED: the server Purchase had NO test - provable, not suspected: commenting out reportPurchaseToMeta left all 950 green. notifyPaid and markRefunded had none at all. Both covered now and the probe re-run: removing that line fails two tests. Also fixed: a guard failing OPEN (the disclosure assertion sat behind a grep of the source it guarded), a flaky health assertion (not.toContain("12") against a body carrying dbMs), SENT logged for any 2xx even with no events_received, and preorders.fb_attrib existing only in production - a rebuild from this repo would have 500d every pre-order. The runbook was half that bug: it said to paste 0001, so a rebuild already missed 0002.

SENIOR QA RETURNED needs-work AND WAS RIGHT ON THE TWO THAT MATTERED. (1) My commit message CLAIMED §8.25-p had been updated to match the new allow-list. It had not: my replacement matched `.neq("status", "paid")` WITH a space and the law had it without one, so the law still documented the bug twenty lines from the constant that replaced it, and CLAUDE.md tells every session to read §8.25 before touching store code. The fulfil.ts module header had the same stale text. Both fixed. (2) The privacy rewrite introduced a NEW false sentence and pinned it with a test - the exact failure it existed to remove. It said the network address and browser "are the two it needs in readable form"; fbp and fbc go verbatim too, so four of the seven user_data fields are unhashed. The copy no longer counts (a category is honest at any payload size; a number stops being true the moment a field is added) and a new test accounts for every unhashed key instead.

MUTATION-TESTED THE FIXES RATHER THAN TRUSTING THEM. The senior QA proved by deletion that the not-payable call sites, alertNotPayable, the orphan re-read and the notifyPaid try/catch were all invisible to the suite: each could be removed with 973/973 still green. All four now have tests, and each was verified by mutation (delete the alert call, rethrow from the catch, revert the allow-list) rather than by inspection. Also fixed the schema-coverage guard, which matched substrings and comments: `dispatch` passed on the words "dispatch queue" in a comment and `payment_id` passed inside `rzp_payment_id`. Comments are stripped and matching is word-boundary now, with both false-positive shapes pinned.
